messages:
anna: heads up — after rolling soft_admit_v2 last night p99 for short sequences (<=64) jumped ~25%. Noticed in canary dashboards. anyone dug in yet?

josh: saw the same on staging -> prod canary. profiler shows queue_age spiking for short seqs. looks like batches are waiting longer to reach token_budget.

ravi: KV cache numbers look fine overall (hit 0.84 -> 0.85) so not likely cache misses causing this. small seq path hit-rate unchanged.

lisa: my guess: token_budget_target was lowered to 384 in the feature flag rollout. that can push runtime to wait to hit budget before flushing which hurts short seq latency.

ken: ops noticed more 429 soft-shed responses too. logs: `2025-11-05T03:11:22Z admit_reject=soft client_id=svc-search reason="soft_headroom_exceeded"` — mostly from bursty low-length traffic.

anna: proposed quick plan: 1) revert token_budget_target => 512 for short_seq policy only; 2) add age-based early-flush: if first_req_age_ms > 15ms flush regardless of token budget; 3) instrument `batch_fill_delay_ms` and `admit_reason` tag. rollout to 5% canary.

josh: +1. sample pseudo for admission check:

```
# pseudo admission (runtime)
if queue_length == 0:
  start_timer()
if first_req_age_ms > AGE_FLUSH_MS:
  flush_batch(reason="age_flush")
elif current_token_count >= token_budget_target:
  flush_batch(reason="budget_full")
elif soft_shed and estimated_latency > latency_slo:
  reject_with_429(retry_after=RETRY_MS)
else:
  continue_batch()
```

lisa: also recommend a soft headroom value (20%) so we don't pack to exact budget — gives room for immediate flushes on age. and for 429s, set `Retry-After: 0.2`s and include a JSON body: `{\"error\":\"server_busy_try_again\",\"admit_reason\":\"soft_shed\"}`. instrument client_id dimension.

ravi: i'll add a small microbench for the KV cache hotpath for seq<=64 to confirm routing isn't adding serialization overhead.

observability-bot: created metric `runtime.batch_fill_delay_ms` and alert `p99_short_seq_latency_increase` at 10% above baseline.

deploy-bot: canary deploy of age-flush + token_budget short_seq=512 -> 5% now.

ken: i'll watch 429 counts and set a temporary alert if > 2x baseline for 5m. also we should update runbook step for soft-shed rollback.

anna: rollback guard: if p99_short_seq > baseline * 1.10 for 10m -> auto rollback the canary. also if client-facing 429s spike beyond threshold revert earlier.

josh: i'll own the experiment, collect end-to-end traces and raw profiler samples. will post perf traces here at +30m.

lisa: one more thought — batching heuristics should prefer age for first-in-batch <-> promote head-of-queue flush when head is old even if budget low. this avoids tail inflation for tiny requests.

anna: agreed. long-term we might add a hybrid objective: minimize cost per-token subject to latency constraints; for now age-first heuristics + soft headroom seems safest.

ravi: adding perf test now. will run 10k requests with seq distribution skewed low and post results.

ken: noted. i'll keep paging on for the next 30m.

josh: :thumbsup: posting initial trace in ~20m.

anna: thanks team. keep comments short — if you need a follow-up meeting DM me and i'll schedule a quick triage.
